title: Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery
summary: extend the sub-scope Import workflow with trusted returned-package overwrite, stale-source, and all-or-nothing protection
content_html:
Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery

Status And Order

Proposed as SRR-2 after both the completed Sub-Scope Returned Package Review Delivery and the planned Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery.

SRR-1 proved that one complete returned package from an exact { scope, sub_scope } collection can reach faithful, immutable Docs Review. SSO-1 first establishes one exact-collection Import control and shared ordinary source target. SRR-2 then extends that workflow with one separately confirmed path from an eligible returned JSON/JSONL package back to the same canonical flat collection.

This is not a Save control in Docs Review and does not broaden ordinary scope-level Docs Import.

Complete Outcome

A local Manage docs_subscope report uses the compact 📥 Import icon and exact mounted-collection workflow introduced by SSO-1. SRR-2 adds trusted returned packages as a separate source type; it does not add a second report button or modal.

The action:

  1. freezes the mounted { scope, sub_scope } collection;
  2. lists only trusted returned packages that match that exact collection and explicitly support return Import;
  3. previews one complete package against current canonical sources;
  4. requires one package-level confirmation;
  5. applies every accepted source update or none; and
  6. rebuilds and refreshes only the owning sub-scope projection.

Import is a collection action. It never consumes checked IDs, the displayed detail document, the parent report document, URL text, the latest staged file, or the package currently open in Docs Review.

Report Toolbar Contract

  • The 📥 button remains the one local management contribution introduced by SSO-1, with Import as its accessible label and title. Public reports receive no control, service probe, or Import module.
  • Import is a sibling toolbar control, not an item in the selection-owned Actions menu. Activating it does not enter selection mode, reveal checkboxes, or change checked IDs.
  • The existing 🔧 Actions control keeps its current behavior: opening it enters selection mode and Prepare package… remains checked-ID-backed.
  • Import availability remains independent of collection rows. SRR-2 adds package availability to the existing exact-collection Import surface without changing ordinary staged-source availability.
  • Activating the button lazily loads a focused sub-scope package workflow using the exact mounted collection and restores focus to the same button on close.
  • The package chooser shows file, configured collection label, and document count. It includes only packages whose trusted scope and sub_scope match the frozen collection and whose supports_return_import is true.
  • No package is silently preselected from another route or workflow. Confirming Import always follows an explicit package choice and reviewed preview.
  • Cancel applies nothing. Failure retains a safe retry path for the same frozen collection and never falls back to the parent scope.
  • Success refreshes the report inventory and rendered detail from the confined sub-scope build. It does not open Source or change the main Index selection.

Package Eligibility

Sub-scope Import is opt-in per configured collection. Analysis/Tags is the first consumer; removing the current blanket blocker must not make every configured sub-scope importable.

For an opted-in sub-scope:

package profile supports_docs_review supports_return_import
document-content true true
document-tree false false

Trusted metadata must retain the exact scope, sub_scope, profile, selected_doc_ids, and prepared source-version map. Returned rows must equal the complete prepared ID set. Missing, extra, duplicate, malformed, cross-collection, or capability-invalid records block the whole package.

Existing sub-scope packages prepared under SRR-1 remain review-only because their trusted metadata says supports_return_import: false. They require regeneration after SRR-2; there is no metadata migration or compatibility fallback.

Canonical Apply Contract

  • Every returned ID must still identify one existing document in the frozen configured child collection. SRR-2 is overwrite-only: it does not create, delete, move, or rename documents.
  • The configured collection remains flat. Non-empty returned hierarchy fields block Import rather than inventing or mutating parent_id.
  • Returned title, summary, and document content may update. Canonical collection metadata not owned by the package—such as group, ui_status, viewable, immutable doc_id, and added_date—is preserved.
  • Trusted prepared source versions are compared with current canonical sources during preview and again immediately before apply. Any stale target refreshes or blocks the plan and requires a new confirmation.
  • Preview is write-free and exposes the complete planned document set. There is no record selection, skip, create/overwrite choice, or partial confirmation.
  • Apply precomputes and validates every target before entering one confined write boundary. A source-write or rebuild failure restores the pre-apply source snapshot and reports no successful Import.
  • The existing sub-scope write/rebuild owner performs the confined projection follow-through. Parent Index, Recent, global search, and other collections remain unchanged.

Ownership

  • The SSO-1 sub-scope contribution retains ownership of the toolbar button, availability projection, and explicit mounted-collection request.
  • The document-report management host retains validation of that request and lazy loading of the shared Import workflow.
  • Existing returned-package listing and trusted validation remain the package discovery and whole-package identity owners.
  • The document-package Import planner and normalized ImportContent boundary are extended with an explicit sub-scope collection target; a second parser or parallel document mutation model is not added.
  • The sub-scope source write/rebuild service owns confined apply, rollback, and generated follow-through.
  • The ordinary Docs Import modal, top-level collection planner, and Docs Review route retain their current behavior.

Boundary

In scope:

  • explicit per-sub-scope returned-package Import opt-in;
  • exact-collection package listing, preview, confirmation, apply, and result;
  • a returned-package source type inside the existing 📥 Import report workflow, still independent of checkbox selection;
  • strict package capability, identity, membership, and flatness validation;
  • overwrite-only title, summary, and content updates;
  • stale-source revalidation and all-or-nothing source/rebuild behavior;
  • confined report refresh and focused service, module, route, and realistic acceptance evidence.

Not in scope:

  • Docs Review Save, Import, or query-string handoff;
  • public Import controls or local-service access;
  • ordinary HTML, DOCX, Markdown, text, media, or top-level package Import redesign;
  • document creation, deletion, hierarchy, moves, doc_id changes, or partial package apply;
  • Tag Registry reads, link repair, title synchronization, or group inference;
  • automatically enabling other sub-scopes; or
  • compatibility support for SRR-1 review-only package metadata.

Delivery Tracker

[ ] SRR-2.0 — Freeze Eligibility And Exact Target

  • [ ] Add explicit collection opt-in and importable sub-scope package projection without weakening false / true validation.
  • [ ] Extend trusted listing and request validation with exact { scope, sub_scope }; retain fail-closed legacy behavior.

[ ] SRR-2.1 — Plan And Apply The Whole Package

  • [ ] Reuse normalized document-package planning for the exact flat collection with overwrite-only field ownership and stale-source validation.
  • [ ] Apply every planned source and confined rebuild or restore the complete pre-apply snapshot.

[ ] SRR-2.2 — Extend Report Import

  • [ ] Add trusted returned-package discovery and chooser state to the existing 📥 Import workflow without a second report button, and preserve Prepare package… checked-ID behavior.
  • [ ] Reuse shared modal, status, busy, retry, and report-refresh boundaries through a focused lazy-loaded workflow.

[ ] SRR-2.3 — Verify And Accept

  • [ ] Prove exact collection targeting, package/canonical staleness, cross-collection rejection, flat metadata preservation, rollback, and unchanged top-level/public behavior with focused fixtures.
  • [ ] Preview and confirm one realistic regenerated Analysis/Tags package, then inspect the canonical sources and confined report projection.

Completion Gate

One explicitly import-enabled returned sub-scope package is chosen from the owning report, revalidated against the exact prepared and current collection, applied completely after one confirmation, and reflected by the confined report rebuild with no parent-scope, public, Docs Review, or partial-write side effect.
